chapter: Long Island years and Battle's estate
title: Battle's career, his scored tributes and recordings
summary: Battle came back from a USO tour with $60,000, bought land, wrote large-scale tributes, and recorded gospel and spirituals.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Now, he did very well for himself as a trumpet player with --
Yeah, well, he made money then, but then what did he do after that?
He went overseas with ______ in the USO show. So they paid the guys a flat salary and they took

men like you never heard of, just guys that could play pretty good and they paid them a flat salary and then they were on (inaudible) and Battles came back and he come back -- when he got back, he had about $60,000. He was hustling over there, during the two years over there with Eisenhower and with the USO band. Then he went up there (inaudible) bought 180 acres of land. He sold it all off piece by piece, 30 acres at a time, like that. But he was throwing me money, he'd say, "Is that all?"
Yeah, do you want me to switch it off?

(Inaudible) one thing at a time (inaudible) scored a lot of it (inaudible), Garner, Tribute to Duke Ellington, Tribute to Benny ______, Don Redman, Tribute to Eddie Durham -- supposed to be my ______ (inaudible). The last year, he wrote ______ songs.
Well, I mean, he did write in all this, but he didn't do anything with it.
No, and he scored it up for like 30-piece bands, fiddles and things and all that.
Yeah, it's good. Anybody could edit it. The only thing is, he's got bad spots in it where it's overloaded and you can't play it. Benny Morton and all those guys

played it. He had the big bands play it. I (inaudible) and he's got a lot of other good material on records out, because in the later six months, he got into a good professional kick and he started going to the professional studios and let them do the recording of groups and things.
Yeah, but what sort of groups did he record?

He did gospel, spirituals, a lot of it was piano and organ combination with a few other things. He had good singers. I got some of it on tape. Some of (inaudible) because Uncle Tom's Cabin's got about ten songs he was searching around and recording people.
